items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the state administrative procedure act, in relation to
improving evaluations of the potential impact of rules on jobs and employment
opportunities
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2839

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the state administrative procedure act, in relation to
improving evaluations of the potential impact of rules on jobs and
employment opportunities

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would make various improvements to the process for evaluating
the potential impact of proposed rules on jobs and employment opportu-
nities. The current process, while useful, does not provide sufficient
information on the quality of jobs that could be gained or lost by
pursuing various policy choices, and does not guarantee that the most
appropriate data and methodologies are used.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends § 201-a of the State Administrative Procedure Act
(SAPA) to revise the process for reviewing the impact of a proposed rule
on jobs and employment opportunities. The following substantive improve-
ments would be made to the process:

*subdivision (2)(b)(v) is amended to require information on measures
that the proposing agency or other state agency have taken or could take
to minimize any adverse impacts on jobs (e.g., by instituting new
apprenticeship or educational programs);

*subdivision (2)(d)(i) is amended to require state agencies to issue
revised job impact statements when it is necessary to correct or supple-
ment information presented in the previous statement that was inadequate
or incomplete;

*subdivision (2) (e) is amended to provide that, if the Commissioners of
Labor and Economic Development have indicated that further evaluation is
needed, an agency that is unable to determine the job impact of a
proposal may not adopt until it has performed the additional analysis or
the statutory time period has run;

*a new subdivision (2)(j) provides that the agency shall make its meth-
odology and data or data sources available for public review and vali-
dation;

*subdivision (6)(a) is amended to clarify that job impact statements do
not need to be prepared for consensus rules; and

*paragraphs (b) & (c) of subdivision (6) are amended to require consid-
eration of the quality of jobs and employment opportunities that could
be affected, including the impact of a rule on average wage levels,
hours and or duration of employment, or other impacts that could repre-
sent a substantial adverse impact on incomes or economic security.

Section 2 through 6 amend various subdivisions of § 202 to better inte-
grate the publication of job impact statements into the statutory
provisions for preparation of rulemaking notices.

Section establishes an effective date.
 
JUSTIFICATION:

When state agencies develop rules and regulations, it is crucial that
the potential impact on current jobs and future employment is thoroughly
analyzed. Overly burdensome regulations can have a devastating impact on
businesses, and economic development throughout the state. This bill
will enable policymakers to design regulatory programs in a manner that
accomplishes desired objectives, while taking into consideration the
impact such regulation will have on current and future employment within
the state.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017-2018: S.3751, Passed Senate
2015-2016: S.6448-A, Veto Memo. 277

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law, and shall apply to any rule
first proposed or adopted on an emergency basis on or after such date.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 66
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2839-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the state administrative procedure act, in relation
      to  improving evaluations of the potential impact of rules on jobs
      and employment opportunities"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the State Administrative Procedure Act (SAPA) to
require additional analysis by State agencies, including requiring State
agencies to identify measures that  other  agencies  deemed  to  have  a
significant  impact  have taken, or could have taken, to address the job
impacts of a proposed rule.
 
  This bill, as drafted, raises the same concerns as a  similar  bill  I
vetoed  in  2016  (Veto  No.  277  of  2016) requiring State agencies to
include any measures that other State agencies have  taken  to  minimize
any  unnecessary  adverse  impacts  on existing jobs would require every
agency to reach out to all other agencies, to find out  what  they  have
done, or could do on any regulation. Many would be completely irrelevant
to  the  issues  or  operational challenges facing the inquiring agency.
This requirement would lengthen  the  rule  implementation  process  and
impose  a  significant  administrative  burden on agencies, particularly
with respect to increased  staffing  resources,  without  providing  the
funding necessary to support that burden, and for minimal, if any, effi-
cacy.
 
  Ensuring proper evaluation of the potential impact on jobs and employ-
ment  opportunities of proposed regulations is an important governmental
function. However, as I noted previously,  SAPA  already  requires  such
reviews  to  evaluate  and  minimize  negative  impacts.  I am therefore
constrained to again veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
